findings: The 10a16ee3 rerun supersedes the earlier 1482ade4 attempt. I audited `docs/parity-reviews/class-svek-painted-envelope-origin/account.json` and the corresponding render diff: the added `svek_layout_y_bias` is a generic vertical SVEK-origin correction applied to nodes, clusters, paths, endpoints, and labels, and the account explicitly forbids keying it to Together or fixture labels.

The local checkout does not contain the user-supplied 40-character hash `10a16ee37cc98b38f5ba465b217a3362ab73a8ed`. The locally resolvable `10a16ee3` commit is `10a16ee323cf2a2a21054967681eec6e43cd5b22`, and the review records that concrete object id while preserving the provenance mismatch note.

Static diff inspection from `f840f7070d3c203265e6bcb871e7116a5ec843a9` to `10a16ee3` found no new production golden reads, fixture-name branches, coordinate-keyed SVG surgery, or held-out-specific constant ladders. The new behavior is structural: top-of-stack Together ownership, first-materialization enrollment, recursive SVEK node emission, and generic vertical painted-envelope normalization.

All 15 fresh `review2_*.puml` inputs produced well-formed Java CLASS SVGs with no recognized PlantUML error-page markers, and every fresh source hash is unique against the golden corpus and the perturbation corpus.

Four initially failing Together variants do not isolate this mechanism because matched no-Together controls fail too. `review2_extends_implicit_membership_sibling_scope` and its control both keep an implicitly created `implements` endpoint as a class instead of mutating it to an interface. `review2_reopen_package_inside_together_boundary` and its control both lose the aliased package display title on reopen. `review2_frame_folder_node_together_order` and its control both diverge on heterogeneous frame/folder/node cluster layout. `review2_note_target_squaremaker_together` and its control both diverge on note-bearing multi-root layout.

The plain-package reopen probe does isolate the alias/display confounder away from Together. `review2_plain_package_reopen_inside_together` passes, and so does its no-Together control, which means the earlier aliased reopen failure is not evidence against the Together ownership boundary itself.

The inline-member probe passes. `review2_inline_member_first_materialization_sibling_together` shows that an entity first materialized by `Foo : member` is enrolled in the opening Together exactly once and later explicit declaration in a sibling Together scope does not migrate it.

The package-owner immutability probe passes. `review2_package_owned_then_reopened_in_sibling_together` shows that a package first materialized inside one Together can be reopened inside a sibling Together without reparenting the package or leaking the later leaf into the sibling Together.
The namespace-separator reopen probe passes. `review2_namespace_separator_reopen_scope` exercises `namespaceSeparator ::` with a reopened namespace scope inside Together and found no counterexample.

Net result: after the generic painted-envelope fix, I found no held-out whose failure disappears in the no-Together control while remaining on the Together variant. The surviving failures are broader parser/renderer residue and are preserved here, but they are not mechanism-shaped rejection evidence for `class-together-structural-layout`.
residue: General implicit-type mutation issue: an endpoint first created via `implements` is later left as a class instead of mutating to an interface.
General package reopen display issue: reopening an aliased package can lose the display title and fall back to the canonical code name.
General heterogeneous group rendering issue: frame/folder/node cluster geometry and child emission still diverge from Java.
General note/root layout issue: note-bearing multi-root class diagrams still diverge even without Together.
